courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course introduces students to the Workplace Hazardous Materials Management System (WHMIS) and WorkSafeBC regulations. Students will apply the regulations to shop safety, hazardous material safety, fire safety, safe work practices, and proper body mechanics in their work environment. ​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

​This course introduces students to the administrative skills, knowledge, and practice necessary to contribute to the operation of an efficient shop. Areas of study include staff responsibilities/roles within a service facility, service department operations, forms and procedures, customer relations and service information systems utilization. This course also provides students with the practical skills required to find employment. Topics covered include resume and cover letter preparation and job search strategies.​ Prerequisite(s): MCTC 1400

​This course is designed to provide students with the theoretical understanding and practical skills related to tools and equipment, the application and safe handling of the tools. All coursework reflects the type of skills encountered in the Motorcycle service industry.​ Prerequisite(s): MCTC 1400

This course introduces students to the fundamental skills related to the handling of heating and welding equipment including safety, equipment shut down and storage, oxy-acetylene torches, and metal inert gas. Students will perform basic Gas Metal Arc Welding/Metal Inert Gas (GMAW/MIG) and Oxyacetylene welding. Students will perform cutting of mild steel and angle iron, oxy-fuel welding, and brazing of mild steel plate. Prerequisite(s): MCTC 1400

​This course introduces students to tire construction; procedures for changing and repairing tubes and tubeless tires, wheel balancing and procedures. The students will also perform basic service procedures on hubs and bearing assemblies as encountered in the Motorcycle repair industry.​ Prerequisite(s): MCTC 1400

​This course introduces students to the fundamental skills, operational principles and service procedures for brake systems that are required to diagnose, service, and repair various types of braking systems including: disc-brakes, drum brake assemblies, and brake hydraulics. ​ Prerequisite(s): MCTC 1400

​This course introduces students to the fundamental skills required to diagnose, service, and repair various types of suspension systems and components, commonly encountered in the Motorcycle service industry. Students will also learn basic frame and chassis design principles, handling and stability problems related to various Motorcycles, including All Terrain Vehicles.​ Prerequisite(s): MCTC 1400

courses.course_name: Basic Principles of Internal Combustion Engines
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course introduces the students to two- and four-cycle internal combustion engine design, commonly encountered in the Motorcycle service industry. Students will also become familiar with lubrication-systems and cooling system operation of the internal combustion engines.​ Prerequisite(s): MCTC 1400

​This course introduces the students to basic electrical principles, electrical circuits, magnetism, and electrical generation. Students will learn how to interpret electrical diagrams, use digital and analog meters, service batteries, charging system, starting systems and component operation. Students will also be introduced to specific electronic diagnostic equipment and retrieve diagnostic trouble codes as well as perform basic service procedures for various electrical components and systems related to Motorcycles.​ Prerequisite(s): MCTC 1400

​This course introduces the students to design and operation of chain, belt and gear drive systems, as well as final drives and differential systems related to various Motorcycles and All-Terrain vehicles.​ Prerequisite(s): MCTC 1400

courses.course_name: Routine Inspection and Maintenance Work Practices
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course introduces students to the fundamental skills related to the use of lubricants and fluids, procedures for measuring levels and condition of fluids, maintenance requirements, identifying sources of leaks, replacement of gaskets and seals, and performing pre-delivery and pre-storage servicing related to Motorcycles.​ Prerequisite(s): MCTC 1400

admission.raw: Scheduled intakes February and September *Scheduled intakes are subject to change Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first qualified basis as long as space remains. When available intakes are full, qualified applicants are wait-listed. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements prior to applying to this program. If you are uncertain or don’t meet the requirements we strongly recommend you complete any applicable Trades Entry Assessments before applying. English language proficiency: one of the following: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent or BCIT English Trades Entry Assessment Math: one of the following: Foundations of Math and Pre-Calculus 10 (50%) or Workplace Math 10 (50%) or Other acceptable BC and Yukon courses or BCIT Math Trades Entry Assessment Please note: This program is also offered in a high school setting; applicants who will be attending a high school site will be required to undergo a criminal record check. Applicants can contact their local police department to obtain the appropriate forms. Please be aware that the outcome of the criminal record check may influence your acceptability at this site. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Recommended for success Potential students with medical or physical disabilities should contact Accessibility Services to arrange an interview with the institute's rehabilitation specialist at 604-451-6963 (telephone interview is acceptable for out of town applicants). High school graduation is recommended by SkilledTradesBC. Please refer to the SkilledTradesBC website for current apprenticeship prerequisite information. International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks.
